Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported within 10 business days. S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, injury, property damage, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a fuller report within 10 business days. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported within 10 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers promptly when an incident presents a credible safety risk, and no later than 5 business days after that determination.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, injury, property damage, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a fuller report within 10 business days. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported within 10 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers promptly when an incident presents a credible safety risk, and no later than 5 business days after that determination. Reports must include known circumstances, model and serial number, and actions taken; updates must be provided as facts are confirmed.

parameters.quote: Each model must undergo a standardized sustained-heat test at 55 °C before market entry, at least every three years, and after a material design change. A failure rate above 5% triggers a corrective-action plan submitted to the regulator and annual retesting until compliant; it does not by itself automatically bar sales. Regulators may impose market restrictions where the evidence indicates an unreasonable safety risk. Full per-model results must be submitted confidentially to the regulator and provided to customers who buy that model, including prospective customers before purchase.

over_limit_consequence.rule: sales must eventually stop above the limit

transition.rule: ≤12 months (any cap ≤7% or none) or ≤36 months with interim ≤7% = acceptable

results_to_customers.rule: customers must get at least pass/fail

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Each model must undergo a standardized sustained-heat test at 55 °C before market entry, at least every three years, and after a material design change. A failure rate above 5% triggers a corrective-action plan submitted to the regulator and annual retesting until compliant; it does not by itself automatically bar sales. Regulators may impose market restrictions where the evidence indicates an unreasonable safety risk. Full per-model results must be submitted confidentially to the regulator and provided to customers who buy that model, including prospective customers before purchase.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a standardized sustained-heat test at 55 °C before market entry, at least every three years, and after a material design change. A failure rate above 5% triggers a corrective-action plan submitted to the regulator and annual retesting until compliant; it does not by itself automatically bar sales. Regulators may impose market restrictions where the evidence indicates an unreasonable safety risk. Full per-model results must be submitted confidentially to the regulator and provided to customers who buy that model, including prospective customers before purchase. Regulators may publish aggregate results, but not an individual company's per-model failure rates.

parameters.quote: New units must support secure remote emergency shut-off no later than three years after this standard takes effect, with appropriate safeguards against unauthorized activation and a local means of safe operation. For units already installed when the standard takes effect, manufacturers must provide a retrofit or equivalent mitigation plan and complete implementation within six years. Regulators may approve documented alternative mitigations where retrofit is impracticable.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: New units must support secure remote emergency shut-off no later than three years after this standard takes effect, with appropriate safeguards against unauthorized activation and a local means of safe operation. For units already installed when the standard takes effect, manufacturers must provide a retrofit or equivalent mitigation plan and complete implementation within six years. Regulators may approve documented alternative mitigations where retrofit is impracticable.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New units must support secure remote emergency shut-off no later than three years after this standard takes effect, with appropriate safeguards against unauthorized activation and a local means of safe operation. For units already installed when the standard takes effect, manufacturers must provide a retrofit or equivalent mitigation plan and complete implementation within six years. Regulators may approve documented alternative mitigations where retrofit is impracticable.

parameters.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard takes effect.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard takes effect.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard takes effect. The suppression system must be designed and tested to contain or mitigate fire propagation, and its performance and maintenance requirements must be documented for customers and regulators.

parameters.quote: A manufacturer must promptly notify regulators and affected customers and initiate a recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. A recall is also required when the regulator determines that a defect or hazard presents an unreasonable risk of serious injury or fire, regardless of the incident rate.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A manufacturer must promptly notify regulators and affected customers and initiate a recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. A recall is also required when the regulator determines that a defect or hazard presents an unreasonable risk of serious injury or fire, regardless of the incident rate.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must provide customers with clear safety notices promptly upon identifying a credible safety risk, including the affected models, known hazards, recommended actions, and how to obtain support; material updates must be sent as facts change. A manufacturer must promptly notify regulators and affected customers and initiate a recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. A recall is also required when the regulator determines that a defect or hazard presents an unreasonable risk of serious injury or fire, regardless of the incident rate. Notices must explain the remedy and remain accessible until the risk is addressed.

judge_section_notes: The final rules keep S2's 5% threshold as a corrective-action trigger rather than an automatic sales bar, allowing Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%) to remain on the market, while per-model results go to customers and regulators but not the public. S3 sets a 3-year deadline for new units and a 6-year retrofit, satisfying Northwind's red line but exceeding the acceptable new-unit window. S5 retains a strict 8/100k mandatory recall and serious-injury recall, which would trigger a recall for Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9/100k); S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months, meeting Halcyon's red line but at high cost to Halcyon.
